svg.title: Developmental milestones and Erikson
svg.desc: One age line from birth to eighteen with the five stages laid along it. Under each stage: what she needs, how she plays, what she fears in hospital, and how you talk to her. Below, the approach that answers most paediatric questions.
svg.text: What she can do and what she fears are the two axes, and almost every question turns on one of them.
give her a job to do
talk to HER, not the parent;
A toddler resisting care gets TWO acceptable choices, never an open question.
"The pink cup or the blue cup?" — not "will you take your medicine?"
bodily harm and mutilation — and she
thinks the illness is a punishment
loss of control; being left out
🩺 THE APPROACHES THAT ARE ALWAYS RIGHT
· Parent present for anything painful, at every age
· Do the painful thing LAST, and never in her bed
· Demonstrate on a doll before you do it to her
· Preschoolers: plain words. "Put you to sleep" and
"take a picture" are terrifying if taken literally
· Adolescents: ask the parent to step out, and mean it
· Let her keep something of her own with her
